input: Read /data/test-results.txt which contains test output in a standard format. Parse it to: 1) Count total tests, passed, and failed. 2) Extract the names of all failing tests. 3) Generate a summary report at /reports/test-summary.md with a header '# Test Summary', a line 'Total: N | Passed: N | Failed: N', and a '## Failures' section listing each failed test. Print the summary.

transcript.final_response:
Parsed `/data/test-results.txt` (12 result lines) and generated the report.

**Counts:** 12 total — 9 passed, 3 failed.

**Failing tests:**
- `test_login_expired_token`
- `test_signup_duplicate_email`
- `test_session_timeout`

The summary report was written to `/reports/test-summary.md` with the `# Test Summary` header, the `Total: 12 | Passed: 9 | Failed: 3` line, and a `## Failures` section listing each failed test as a bullet. Its contents are printed above.
tool_calls:
mkdir -p /reports
awk '
$1 == "PASS" { passed++; next }
$1 == "FAIL" { failed++; fails[failed] = $2 }
END {
  total = passed + failed
  out = "/reports/test-summary.md"
  print "# Test Summary" > out
  print "" > out
  printf "Total: %d | Passed: %d | Failed: %d\n", total, passed, failed > out
  print "" > out
  print "## Failures" > out
  for (i = 1; i <= failed; i++) print "- " fails[i] > out
}' /data/test-results.txt
cat /reports/test-summary.md
